the development of a new method for the generation of stable hybridomas.
the development and application of electrofusion to the generation of monoclonal antibodies.
the development of an electrofusion system that will be useful for the efficient production of stable hybridoma cell lines for the purpose of monoclonal antibody production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrofusion protocol described herein, which is a modification of the conventional protocol, is the most efficient electrofusion protocol for generating stable hybridomas.

the electrofusion of cells in the presence of calcium ions, magnesium ions, bovine serum albumine and a weakly conducting fusion medium, followed by application of high field pulses at a temperature of 25 degrees C in helical chambers is the most efficient protocol for the production of stable hybridoma cells secreting monoclonal antibodies.

the conventional electrofusion procedure can produce high numbers of hybridomas secreting specific antibodies with high efficiency and that the procedure can be optimized to produce hybridomas at a rate of up to 2.45 hybridoma cells per 10(4) splenocyte input cells.

we have developed an electrofusion procedure that is simple, rapid and highly efficient in the generation of hybridoma cells secreting specific antibodies.
the use of the electrofusion technique to generate stable antibody secreting hybridomas can be optimized by the application of a single set of parameters.
electrofusion is an excellent technique for generating hybridomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrofusion protocol is not as complicated as it seems.
the conventional electrofusion protocol can be used to generate a large number of stable hybridomas secreting monoclonal antibodies of the desired specificity.
the electrofusion technique is a simple, efficient and cost effective method for producing hybridomas.
